about: #4628: each surviving det-port mutant stated `equivalent` or `unreachable`, with the Java change and why it cannot alter observable behaviour; proposed in a PR, reviewed by the owner. A run that kills a stated mutant fails (the claim was wrong). Ids are mutation.py's; before / after are the Java line.

verdicts.equivalent: the change cannot alter anything the program shows (output, screen, files, COMMAREA, abend)
verdicts.unreachable: no input of the program reaches the changed code
verdicts.undefined-by-ibm: only non-digit data in a numeric USAGE DISPLAY item kills it, and IBM documents no result for that
verdicts.harness-gap: the change alters behaviour the proof runs but does not compare (open: the harness must)
verdicts.case-gap: an input the case lacks would kill it (open: strengthen the case)

survivors.reason: The initial image literal for FD CARDFILE-REC in Cbact02cService is dead because 1000-CARDFILE-GET-NEXT executes READ into CARD-RECORD before any buffer read.
The initial image literal for CARD-RECORD is dead because 1000-CARDFILE-GET-NEXT unconditionally overwrites CARD-RECORD via READ CARDFILE INTO CARD-RECORD prior to DISPLAY.
The initial image literal for CARDFILE-STATUS is dead because 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN executes OPEN INPUT CARDFILE which populates CARDFILE-STATUS before any condition check.
The initial image literal for IO-STATUS is dead because IO-STATUS is only read in 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, which is always preceded by a MOVE to IO-STATUS.
The initial image literal for TWO-BYTES-BINARY is dead because 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS explicitly executes Cobol.move(0, TWO_BYTES_BINARY) before use.
The initial image literal for IO-STATUS-04 is dead because 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS overwrites all four characters of IO-STATUS-04 before displaying it.

survivors.before: private final Field f29_GG_RETURN_CODE = Field.binary(s_GG_RETURN_CODE, 0, 4, 0, true, false);
survivors.after: private final Field f29_GG_RETURN_CODE = Field.binary(s_GG_RETURN_CODE, 0, 4, 1, true, false);
survivors.reason: f29_GG_RETURN_CODE is only read from s_GG_RETURN_CODE whose initial image is all zero and never written; any binary window read evaluates to 0.
The repository id_CardRecord helper is registered for findById queries, but CBACT02C executes sequential batch reads via findAll, so findById is never invoked.
The initialState arraycopy for FD CARDFILE-REC is dead because 1000-CARDFILE-GET-NEXT populates the buffer from CARDFILE before any read.
The initialState arraycopy for CARD-RECORD is dead because 1000-CARDFILE-GET-NEXT unconditionally reads the next sequential record into CARD-RECORD before 1100-DISPLAY.
The initialState arraycopy for CARDFILE-STATUS is dead because 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN immediately issues OPEN INPUT CARDFILE which sets CARDFILE-STATUS.
The initialState arraycopy for IO-STATUS is dead because IO-STATUS is only read in 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, which is always preceded by MOVE to IO-STATUS.
The initialState arraycopy for IO-STATUS-04 is dead because 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS explicitly formats all four bytes before DISPLAY.
s_GG_RETURN_CODE is all zeros and its fields are read-only; restoring its initial image in initialState() has no observable effect.
Every read of f27_ABCODE in 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM follows an unconditional store of 999 into ABCODE, so the initial zero store is never read.
Omitting initialState() in the constructor has no observable effect because all working storage variables and status buffers are initialized before use.
Paragraph 5 is 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM which terminates execution unconditionally via CobolAbend.user, so paragraph 6 in the PERFORM range is never reached.
Calling super with null container references in the DetService subclass constructor is a no-op that performs no runtime state registration.

survivors.reason: The key length parameter in DetFiles.Indexed is only used for index key extraction on random access, but CBACT02C reads CARDFILE sequentially via findAll.
In the run() entry point, extending the PERFORM range from paragraph 0 thru 5 to paragraph 0 thru 6 cannot reach paragraph 6 because paragraph 5 abends unconditionally.
Restoring the prior numproc PFD state in the finally block of the service runner has no observable effect because the JVM terminates after batch job completion.
Initializing performDepth to 1 instead of 0 in Cbact02cService has no observable effect because the performThru array has capacity 64 and call depth never exceeds 2.
The performThru array expansion in perform() is guarded by mine >= performThru.length (initial capacity 64), which is never reached since perform depth never exceeds 2.
The loop condition d < 0 in perform() is never reached because all PERFORM calls in CBACT02C execute paragraphs that exit without active thru ranges.
The perform loop tail condition d > 0 is never evaluated because CBACT02C only uses single-paragraph perform invocations where i == thru.
In perform(), the reverse search loop tail is entered only when a paragraph returns with i != thru, which no PERFORM statement in CBACT02C does.
In perform(), the increment d++ in the loop tail is never executed because paragraph returns in CBACT02C never satisfy i != thru.
In perform(), inverting the performThru match condition is unreachable because the enclosing loop is never entered when i == thru.
In perform(), testing performThru[d] != i in the search loop is unreachable because CBACT02C performs are simple single-paragraph invocations.
In perform(), testing next < 6 in the paragraph bounds check is unreachable because CBACT02C perform statements never return with i != thru.
In perform(), inverting next >= 6 in the paragraph bounds check is unreachable because the loop tail is only entered when i != thru.
In perform(), testing next > 6 is unreachable because the paragraph dispatcher loop tail is never entered for single-paragraph performs.
In perform(), testing e.depth == mine in the PerformExit handler is unreachable because PerformExit is never thrown in CBACT02C.
In perform(), testing e.depth != mine in the PerformExit catch block is unreachable because PerformExit is never thrown in CBACT02C.
Restoring performDepth in the finally block of perform() has no observable effect because performDepth is only used internally for stack frame tracking upon paragraph exit.
In the paragraph dispatch switch of perform(), the default arm is unreachable because all paragraph indices in CBACT02C are between 0 and 5.
Line 250 follows an unconditional if (true) throw new Goback(); in the top-level dispatch, so the trailing return statement is never reached.
f25_APPL_RESULT is set to 0L at the start of paragraph 0, but 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN immediately assigns 0L to APPL-RESULT, so deleting this assignment has no effect.

In paragraph 0, perform(4, 4) executes 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE; if extended to paragraph 5 (9999-ABEND-PROGRAM), 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE on normal end completes with CARDFILE-STATUS 00 and falls into 9999 only if not stopped, but paragraph 0 throws Goback() immediately following.
In 0000-CARDFILE-OPEN, f25_APPL_RESULT is set to 8L, but on successful OPEN it remains 0L and on failure it is immediately overwritten with 12L before abend.
In DetFiles.Indexed.open(mode), sequential input datasets ignore the mode string and open in read mode regardless of whether mode is INPUT or XNPUT.
In 1000-CARDFILE-GET-NEXT at end of file, perform(4, 4) closes CARDFILE and paragraph 0 issues Goback(); extending thru 5 has no effect because execution halts.
In 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE, adding zero versus subtracting zero from BigDecimal constant D8 (8) is an arithmetic identity producing the exact same numeric value 8.
In 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE, storing 8 into APPL-RESULT is dead because successful CLOSE executes SUBTRACT APPL-RESULT FROM APPL-RESULT (setting it to 0), and error CLOSE sets 12.
In 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE error path, adding zero versus subtracting zero from constant D12 (12) produces identical value 12.
In 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE error path, setting APPL-RESULT to 12 is followed immediately by PERFORM 9910 and PERFORM 9999 which abends without APPL-RESULT ever being read.
In 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM, the routine name string passed to CobolAbend.user is informational and does not alter the abend code 999 or any observable output.
In 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, IO-STAT1 is moved to byte 1 of IO-STATUS-04; shifting to byte 2 is overwritten by the subsequent formatting of IO-STAT2 before display.
